messages:
alex_customer: Hey team — running into a burst of 429s and weird billing spikes during a long-context job. Using rwd-extended-64k, ~120 req/min sustained for a few minutes, many requests ~50-60k tokens input. Errors start after ~30s into the job window, then some calls succeed. Billing dashboard shows a sudden token jump compared to baseline. Anyone seen this pattern?

sai (support): Sorry you hit this, alex. Can you paste a minimal repro curl (no secrets) and the raw response headers/body when you get a 429? Also which SDK/version and region?

alex_customer: yes — repro below (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-extended-64k","input":"<very long doc>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Response (truncated):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 60
x-rwd-rpm-limit: 180
x-rwd-rpm-remaining: 3
x-rwd-tpm-limit: 600000
x-rwd-tpm-remaining: 12000
x-rwd-concurrency-limit: 8
x-rwd-concurrency-remaining: 0
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "per-model concurrency exceeded for rwd-extended-64k" }
```
Looks like concurrency is the bottleneck but RPM also low remaining. Billing shows lots of tokens billed even for retried calls — is that expected?

jonathan.eng: Thanks for the repro. Two things to call out: 1) long-context requests consume more token budget server-side (input+output and internal KV/cache billing) — so TPM is hit faster. 2) Our per-model concurrency window is effectively smaller for very large contexts because each inflight request holds resources longer (KV cache, memory). So even if nominal concurrency=8, practical throughput drops.

maria.ops: Also check client-side retries. If your client retries immediately on 429 without exponential backoff, you can amplify billing because each retry recharges token usage. Try to capture request IDs from responses to correlate in billing logs.

alex_customer: good to know. Can you confirm how tokens are counted — is it input + output (both) and do server retries count?

jonathan.eng: Yes, token billing = input + output + small server-side overhead for very long contexts (that overhead is included in TPM). Retries are billed as separate requests. If you re-send the same huge payload multiple times, each attempt is charged.

jonathan.eng: Quick mitigation suggestions: reduce concurrency from your client (cap to ~6 for 64k context), add exponential backoff with jitter (start 500ms, cap 30s), and prefer streaming so you can early-abort when you detect client-side limits. For steady high throughput with large contexts, Dedicated capacity is the robust solution.

sai (support): We can also temporarily raise your per-model RPM/TPM/concurrency for a short window while you validate — will need account owner approval. If you want, share request IDs or open a support ticket with billing attached and we can correlate the spike.

alex_customer: Is there any per-model flag to opt into a higher-concurrency variant or a fallback model that uses sharded KV so long contexts are cheaper?

jonathan.eng: We have two supported patterns: 1) use rwd-extended-64k but with caching/prefix-KV enabled (client-side token reuse reduces TPM). 2) fallback routing: when concurrency is tight, route to rwd-large-32k (cheaper) or a quantized variant. Routing requires setting a rollout policy in Console or via the API routing config.

maria.ops: For billing spikes, we can check whether retries contributed. If you send a sample request ID (from X-Request-Id header) and approximate timeframe, we can pull exact token accounting and advise credits if it was inadvertent.

alex_customer: Thanks — I'll collect a few X-Request-Id values and timeframe and open the ticket. Meanwhile will throttle concurrency and add backoff. Appreciate the tips :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Note: infra change last night increased per-model RPM in region eu-west-1 from 160 -> 180 for rwd-extended-64k (was a temporary test). If you still see limits after throttling let us know.

billing-bot: FYI — queued billing audit for account acme-corp at 2025-04-02T14:30Z for anomalous token spike.

alex_customer: Awesome, thanks all. Will follow up with request IDs in the ticket.
